title: Intrinsic Nambu finite directions, inverse-Hessian cone and mixed Hodge certificates

newly_cached_primary_context.title: The Legendre potential and the gradient case of the differential Galois criterion for the Jacobian conjecture
newly_cached_primary_context.portions_inspected: Section 2 Lemma 2.1; Section 4 Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.7 and Remark 4.8; abstract and scope. The definition and actual Legendre-energy derivative identity are used and fully reproved.
newly_cached_primary_context.role: Primary context and attribution for Nambu derivations and the single Legendre-energy identity. The direction-specific finite-orbit test, norm exclusion of nonzero eigenvalues, plane slice argument, HC4 two-or-four direction space, inverse-Hessian cone rigidity and mixed-trace criterion are written directly using retained Tang/HX0 inputs.

HC4MYHX0 relative algebraic closure of a nowhere-critical polynomial parameter

direct_proof_arguments: Keller field norm turns a hypothetical constant eigenvalue into an impossible constant logarithmic derivative of a rational target function
local finiteness has only zero eigenvalues and hence is local nilpotence for every constant Nambu direction
one locally finite plane direction has a slice and regular-parameter constants, generating the whole plane source ring
commuting Nambu derivatives of the actual Legendre energy are the source coordinates, so one finite energy orbit implies local finiteness on the whole source ring
in Tang coordinates locally finite directions are precisely the annihilator of the unique affine plane, unless the entire gradient is invertible
zero inverse-Hessian square kills second Nambu derivatives of every coordinate and supplies an explicit polynomial quasi-translation
under nonautomorphy the exact constant inverse-Hessian quadratic cone equals the same linear two-plane
any supplied linear zero-square two-plane reconstructs the actual cotangent coefficient pair by unit-determinant block inversion, without using Tang for this converse
pure Hodge traces and finite-energy directions may be combined in one three-direction certificate
an explicit automorphic quartic-base potential has exactly a linear two-plane cone but extra finite-energy directions, so the cone condition is not a converse
the canonical relative polynomial slice is locally nilpotent exactly at original Keller field degree one
